alt: Two general criteria, being intelligible and generally using language appropriate to the formal setting, must both be met before any of Pass, Merit or Distinction can be awarded. AO9 assesses using spoken Standard English effectively in speeches and presentations.
caption: Intelligibility and generally appropriate language are needed for any grade.

after: ## What Standard English is, and is not
alt: A grid with grammar (standard or non-standard) across and register (formal or informal) down. A formal presentation needs standard grammar and formal register. “I’m knackered” is standard but informal; “We was invited” is non-standard however formally it is delivered. Standard English can be spoken in any accent, and choosing the right variety is code-switching.
caption: A formal talk needs Standard English grammar and a formal register, in any accent.

alt: A table of nine areas with non-standard examples and Standard English equivalents, for example “we was” to “we were”, “I was sat” to “I was sitting”, “them results” to “those results”, “the man what helped us” to “the man who helped us” and “innit” to “isn’t it”.
caption: In a formal presentation, use the Standard English form.

alt: Three overcorrections and their Standard English forms: “between you and I” becomes “between you and me”, “send it to myself” becomes “send it to me”, and “whom is responsible?” becomes “who is responsible?”. A quick test removes the other person: “between… me” and “I went” sound natural.
caption: Overcorrecting to sound formal produces errors too.

after: ## Spoken Standard English is still speech
alt: Acceptable in formal speech: contractions in moderation, discourse markers such as “Right, let’s begin”, and occasional self-correction. Undermining AO9: persistent non-standard grammar, heavy fillers such as “like” and “basically”, and slang. To keep control: rehearse aloud, know your habits, pause instead of filling, and slow down.
caption: Sound like a confident speaker, not a textbook.

after: ## Worked example: revising a spoken passage
alt: A table of changes to the survey transcript: “me and Leah done” becomes “Leah and I carried out”, “we was” becomes “we were”, “don’t never… no more” becomes “no longer… at all”, “Them benches is all broke” becomes “the benches are broken”, and fillers, slang and “innit” are removed. The accent stays the same.
caption: Fix the grammar and vocabulary; keep the accent.
